question: How Do I Create a Custom 404 Page With Elementor?
metaDescription: Create a 404 template in Elementor Pro's Theme Builder, design it visually, and set its display condition to the built-in "404 Page" option.
shortAnswer: With Elementor Pro's Theme Builder, creating a new template and choosing the "404 Page" type (or setting a general Single/Archive template's display condition specifically to "404 Page") lets you design a fully custom not-found page visually — helpful navigation links, a search bar, and on-brand messaging — replacing whatever plain default the active theme would otherwise show.

image.alt: A custom-designed 404 page built through Elementor's Theme Builder, replacing the theme's plain default

bodyHtml:
How a Custom 404 Template Works

Once created and published with its display condition set to 404 Page, the Theme Builder template takes over any time WordPress would otherwise show its default not-found response, replacing the theme's plain version site-wide. It's designed with the same visual editor as any other page, giving full control over layout and content rather than being limited to whatever customization the active theme's own 404 template allows.

What a Good 404 Page Includes

  • Clear, friendly messaging confirming the requested page wasn't found, without being overly apologetic or confusing.
  • A search bar, helping a visitor who mistyped a URL or followed an outdated link find what they were actually looking for.
  • Links to key pages (homepage, popular categories, main navigation) giving the visitor an obvious next step rather than a dead end.
  • Consistent branding and design matching the rest of the site, rather than the jarring plain-text default many themes fall back to.

Setting This Up

  1. Go to Templates → Theme Builder and create a new template, choosing the 404 Page type if available, or setting the appropriate display condition manually.
  2. Design the page visually, including a search bar and helpful navigation links.
  3. Publish the template and test by visiting a genuinely non-existent URL on the live site.

Need a custom 404 page or full Theme Builder setup built properly? See Elementor customization.
